skill.name: structural-search
skill.description: Use ast-grep structural search to find semantic code patterns, inspect security issues, and plan safer refactors across multiple languages.
skill.summary: Use ast-grep to find and refactor code by syntax tree structure.

security_audit.summary: All 57 static findings were false positives after file-context review. The flagged snippets are ast-grep search examples, Markdown code spans, placeholder URLs, or YAML documentation rather than executable malicious behavior. No prompt injection or data exfiltration intent was found.

remediation.issue: Shell pipeline examples use xargs in documentation.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer null-delimited examples or ast-grep file filters to reduce filename handling risk.

remediation.issue: Security pattern examples resemble dangerous code to static scanners.
remediation.suggestion: Label each block as search patterns, not executable application code.

remediation.issue: Rewrite examples can change project files.
remediation.suggestion: Keep preview guidance near every rewrite command and require user confirmation before applying changes.

content.user_title: Find Code Patterns with AST Search
content.value_statement: Regex searches miss code meaning and create noisy results. This skill helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code use ast-grep for precise structural code search.
actual_capabilities: Provides ast-grep examples for JavaScript, TypeScript, Python, Go, and Rust.
Finds function calls, imports, class definitions, hooks, async usage, and error handling patterns.
Documents security searches for eval, innerHTML, hardcoded secrets, command execution, and unsafe deserialization.
Shows reusable YAML rules, rule testing, pre-commit hooks, and CI integration patterns.
Supports refactoring workflows with preview and rewrite examples.
limitations: Requires the ast-grep CLI to be installed before use.
Pattern accuracy depends on the target language parser and code syntax.
Rewrite commands can modify files and should be reviewed before use.
Security matches are candidates that still need human validation.

use_cases.title: Review React Code Before Release
use_cases.description: Find hook usage, console logging, unsafe DOM writes, and import patterns across a TypeScript frontend.

use_cases.title: Triage Python Security Patterns
use_cases.description: Locate command execution, unsafe deserialization, hardcoded credentials, and risky file operations for focused review.

use_cases.title: Create Repeatable CI Checks
use_cases.description: Build ast-grep YAML rules and test workflows for pre-commit hooks or CI security scans.

prompt_templates.title: Find a Function Call
prompt_templates.prompt: Use structural-search to find console logging in this project. Show the ast-grep pattern, likely files, and next review steps.

prompt_templates.title: Search React Hooks
prompt_templates.prompt: Use structural-search to find React state and effect hooks. Group results by file and call out patterns that need review.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Safe Refactor
prompt_templates.prompt: Use structural-search to preview replacing var declarations with const in TypeScript. Show risks and ask before any rewrite.

prompt_templates.title: Build Security Rules
prompt_templates.prompt: Use structural-search to design ast-grep rules for eval, innerHTML, and hardcoded secrets. Include testing and CI guidance.

output_examples.input: Find every console logging call before release.
output_examples.output: The response names the structural search pattern, groups matching files, and recommends previewing removals before any rewrite.

output_examples.input: Check this Python service for unsafe deserialization.
output_examples.output: The response lists pickle-related matches to inspect, explains why each pattern matters, and separates confirmed issues from review items.
The response gives a structural search plan, expected match categories, and a safe rewrite preview workflow.

best_practices: Run searches in preview mode before using rewrite commands.
Pair structural matches with human review for security findings.
Limit searches by language or directory on large repositories.
anti_patterns: Do not treat every structural match as a confirmed bug without context.
Do not run repository-wide rewrite commands without reviewing a preview.
Do not use broad patterns when a language-specific pattern is available.

faq.question: Does this skill install ast-grep?
faq.answer: No. It assumes the sg CLI is installed before use.

faq.question: Can it change files?
faq.answer: It can suggest ast-grep rewrite commands. Review previews before applying rewrite commands.

faq.question: Which languages are covered?
faq.answer: The references cover JavaScript, TypeScript, Python, Go, and Rust examples.

faq.question: Is this a security scanner?
faq.answer: It provides patterns that can find risky code. Results still need human triage.

faq.question: Why use structural search instead of regex?
faq.answer: Structural search matches syntax tree shapes, so it can find code patterns with less text noise.

faq.question: Can Claude Code or Codex use it?
faq.answer: Yes. It documents prompts and commands for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.
